Abstract Motor Efficiency App

The abstract motor efficiency app visualizes the electric power conversion efficiency contours of the abstract motor model. The model is used by Motor & Drive (System-Level) block (Simscape Electrical) and Motor & Drive block (Simscape Driveline).
The abstract motor model represents a system-level motor drive unit (MDU) consisting of an electric motor and a controller. The model parameterizes the electrical efficiency at a single measurement point and can estimate overall electrical losses including torque-dependent copper winding losses, speed-dependent iron (eddy current) losses, and a constant loses that can exist within the MDU system.

Open the app

AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp opens the app.
% Open the app with all defaults.
AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp
AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp(AppParameterFileName=<file_name>, AppParameterStructName=<struct_name>) opens the app by first evaluating the specified <file_name> parameter file and then loading the specified <struct_name> struct from the base workspace to the app. These options correspond to the Parameter file and the Variable name in the app. The field names of the struct must match the app's parameter names as shown in the table.

For convenience, use AbstractMotorEfficiencyAppParameters to get predefined struct fields for a struct. For example, create a script as follows and save it as motor_parameters.m.
% Create an app parameters object. This enables the tab-completion to find and edit properties.
MotorParams = bevutil1.app.AbstractMotorEfficiency.AbstractMotorEfficiencyAppParameters;
 
MotorParams.MaxAngularSpeedMode = "auto";
MotorParams.MaxTorque = simscape.Value(260, "N*m");
MotorParams.MaxPower = simscape.Value(55, "kW");
 
MotorParams.ElectricalEfficiencyPercent = 95;
MotorParams.MeasuredAngularSpeed = simscape.Value(2000, "rpm");
MotorParams.MeasuredTorque = simscape.Value(50, "N*m");
MotorParams.MeasuredIronLosses = simscape.Value(55, "W");
MotorParams.FixedLosses = simscape.Value(40, "W");
 
MotorParams.PlotAutoRange = "on";
MotorParams.PlotAngularSpeedUpperBound = simscape.Value(12000, "rpm");
MotorParams.PlotTorqueUpperBound = simscape.Value(300, "N*m");
MotorParams.PlotContourLevelsPercent = [1, 60, 80, 90, 96, 99];
MotorParams.PlotPowers = simscape.Value([10, 50, 100, 150], "kW");
Then open the app with the parameter file and the struct.
% Specified script file (*.m) must be on the MATLAB path.
AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp( ...
AppParameterFileName = which("motor_parameters.m"), ...
AppParameterStructName = "MotorParams" )
AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp(AppParameterStructName=<struct_name>) opens the app by reading the specified <struct_name> struct from the base workspace. The struct must exist in the base workspace.
% The MotorParams struct must exist in the base workspace.
AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp(AppParameterStructName="MotorParams")
AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp(BlockPath=<block_path>) opens the app by opening the specified model and loading block parameters from the specified vehicle block.
% The app opens the specified model and then loads block parameters from the specified block.
AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp(BlockPath="my_model/Motor & Drive")
AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp(ModelName=<model_name>) opens the app by opening the specified model and loading block parameters from a block in the model. If there are more than two vehicle blocks, the first one is used.
% Supported blocks must exist in the specified model.
AbstractMotorEfficiencyApp(ModelName="my_model")

The single efficiency measurement model is a model to consider electrical power losses due to iron losses, copper losses, and fixed losses as an electrical system within an electric motor. Thus, it does not deal with the rotor damping.

Notes on the maximum motor speed

Maximum motor speed is not a parameter of the abstract motor model, and the Motor & Drive blocks do not have the maximum speed as a parameter, but it is typically constrained by higher-level system requirements.
For example, in the road vehicle applications, the vehicle top speed and a few other vehicle specs determine the maximum motor speed. Let V, R, G be vehicle top speed, tire rolling radius, and reduction gear ratio, respectively. Then the maximum motor speed is determined by
.
Example: When V = 180 km/h (112 mph), R = 30 cm (12 in), G = 1/10, then = 15,915 rpm.

Motor & Drive (System Level) block (Simscape Electrical)

Configure the Motor & Drive (System Level) block as follows.
  • Electrical Torque > Parameterized by: Maximum torque and power
  • Electrical Losses > Parameterize losses by: Single efficiency measurement
Then, use the abstract motor efficiency app or the following function to visualize the power conversion efficiency map.
bevutil1.app.AbstractMotorEfficiency.plotAbstractMotorEfficiency(...
DataSource = "direct", ...
MaxAngularSpeedMode = "specify", ...
MaxAngularSpeed = simscape.Value(17000, "rpm"), ...
... block parameters
MaxTorque = simscape.Value(160, "N*m"), ...
MaxPower = simscape.Value(55, "kW"), ...
ElectricalEfficiencyPercent = 95, ...
MeasuredAngularSpeed = simscape.Value(2000, "rpm"), ...
MeasuredTorque = simscape.Value(50, "N*m"), ...
MeasuredIronLoss = simscape.Value(55, "W"), ...
FixedLoss = simscape.Value(40, "W"), ...
... visualization parameters
PlotAutoRange = "off", ...
PlotAngularSpeedUpperBound = simscape.Value(18000, "rpm"), ...
PlotTorqueUpperBound = simscape.Value(170, "N*m"), ...
PlotContourLevelsPercent = [1 60 80 90 94 96 98], ...
PlotPowers = simscape.Value([10, 50, 100], "kW"), ...
PlotResolution = 500)

Motor & Drive block (Simscape Driveline)

Abstract motor model with the following settings corresponds to the Motor & Drive block.
  • Iron losses at electrical efficiency measurement point, = 0
  • Fixed losses for electrical losses, = 0
  • Rotor damping coefficient, = 0
The block ignores the speed-dependent iron (eddy current) losses, but it considers the torque-dependent copper-wind losses.
bevutil1.app.AbstractMotorEfficiency.plotAbstractMotorEfficiency(...
DataSource = "direct", ...
MaxAngularSpeedMode = "specify", ...
MaxAngularSpeed = simscape.Value(17000, "rpm"), ...
... block parameters
MaxTorque = simscape.Value(160, "N*m"), ...
MaxPower = simscape.Value(55, "kW"), ...
ElectricalEfficiencyPercent = 95, ...
MeasuredAngularSpeed = simscape.Value(2000, "rpm"), ...
MeasuredTorque = simscape.Value(50, "N*m"), ...
MeasuredIronLoss = simscape.Value(0, "W"), ... 0 in the Motor & Drive block
FixedLoss = simscape.Value(0, "W"), ... 0 in the Motor & Drive block
... visualization parameters
PlotAutoRange = "off", ...
PlotAngularSpeedUpperBound = simscape.Value(18000, "rpm"), ...
PlotTorqueUpperBound = simscape.Value(170, "N*m"), ...
PlotContourLevelsPercent = [1 60 80 90 94 96 98], ...
PlotPowers = simscape.Value([10, 50, 100], "kW"), ...
PlotResolution = 500)

Ideal motor

By setting the overall efficiency to 100 %, the abstract motor model becomes an ideal (lossless) motor where the power conversion has no losses in all operating region.
bevutil1.app.AbstractMotorEfficiency.plotAbstractMotorEfficiency(...
DataSource = "direct", ...
MaxAngularSpeedMode = "specify", ...
MaxAngularSpeed = simscape.Value(17000, "rpm"), ...
... block parameters
MaxTorque = simscape.Value(160, "N*m"), ...
MaxPower = simscape.Value(55, "kW"), ...
ElectricalEfficiencyPercent = 100, ... ideal motor
PlotAutoRange = "off", ...
PlotAngularSpeedUpperBound = simscape.Value(18000, "rpm"), ...
PlotTorqueUpperBound = simscape.Value(170, "N*m"), ...
PlotContourLevelsPercent = [1 98 99], ...
PlotPowers = simscape.Value([10, 50, 100], "kW"), ...
PlotResolution = 500)
